eventMetadata.context_description: The 10-year Treasury yield surged to 4.44% on April 29 following the Federal Reserve's April 28-29 FOMC meeting, where policymakers held interest rates steady amid persistent inflation pressures and robust economic data, dashing hopes for near-term rate cuts. This marked a climb from 4.31% earlier in the week, driven by rising oil prices, hawkish comments from Fed Chair Powell, and stronger-than-expected GDP growth signals. Traders now eye the April 30 Employment Cost Index release for wage inflation insights, alongside ongoing quantitative tightening and fiscal deficit concerns, as key factors that could push yields higher or trigger a pullback before month-end resolution. Historical patterns show yields often peak post-FOMC amid shifting rate cut odds.

events.title: Japan 10Y Bond Yield: End of 2026
events.description:
This market will resolve according to the 10-year Japanese government bond (JGB) yield on the last reported day of 2026, as reported by the Japanese Ministry of Finance.

If the reported value falls exactly between two brackets, this market will resolve to the higher range bracket.

The resolution source for this market will be the Japanese Ministry of Finance’s “Interest Rate” data for Japanese Government Bonds found at (https://www.mof.go.jp/english/policy/jgbs/reference/interest_rate/index.htm). The resolution will be based on the value listed in the column labelled “10Y” in row corresponding to the latest reported date of 2026. 

The latest reported date will be confirmed once the Japanese Ministry of Finance publishes its first 10-year government bond yield for a 2027 date. The last 2026 date published before that point will be treated as the final reported date of 2026. If the Ministry of Finance has not published any 2027 yield data for the specified date by January 31, 2027, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve using the most recent 2026 yield published as of that date.

eventMetadata.context_description: Japan 10-year government bond yields currently trade near 2.80 percent following a rapid climb of more than 120 basis points over the past year, driven by the Bank of Japan’s June policy rate hike to 1.00 percent and subsequent decision to hold steady amid upwardly revised core inflation forecasts for fiscal 2026. Persistent price pressures from yen depreciation, elevated energy costs linked to Middle East tensions, and robust global demand have prompted hawkish BOJ communications that signal additional tightening ahead. These dynamics have concentrated trader sentiment around the 2.6–3.0 percent range for year-end 2026, with the closely matched leading outcomes reflecting uncertainty over the pace of further normalization versus potential growth moderation or geopolitical easing that could cap yields. Upcoming BOJ meetings and inflation data releases will remain key swing factors.

events.title: California Immunology Research Bond Proposition
events.description:
Proposition 38 is a California ballot measure currently scheduled for voting on November 3, 2026. It would allow the state to borrow $8.4 billion in debt to research immune system-based technologies for treating conditions including cancer, heart disease and Alzheimer’s.

This market will resolve to “Yes” if the specified ballot measure is approved by a majority of voters at the California statewide general election currently scheduled for November 3, 2026. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No.”

If voting on the specified ballot measure does not occur, or the results thereof are not known definitively, by March 31, 2027, this market will resolve to “No”.

This market will resolve based on a consensus of credible reporting. If there is ambiguity, this market will resolve solely based on official information from the State of California, including the California Secretary of State (https://www.sos.ca.gov/).

eventMetadata.context_description: California voters will decide Proposition 38 on the November 2026 ballot, which would authorize $8.4 billion in general obligation bonds for immunology and immunotherapy research, with at least half directed to cancer, heart disease, and Alzheimer’s studies. The measure qualified in June 2026 after signature gathering and allocates roughly half the proceeds to a designated University of California-affiliated nonprofit institute selected by the Department of Public Health, with the balance awarded via competitive grants to California public and nonprofit institutions. Primary backing comes from philanthropist Gary Michelson, who has committed substantial private funding to launch a related UCLA-affiliated center. Trader pricing near 57% for passage reflects typical early support for targeted medical research bonds alongside caution over added General Fund debt service and competition with other 2026 fiscal priorities.

If at any point it becomes impossible for a listed partnership to win the 2026 PPA: Sacramento Open Mixed Doubles Tournament per the rules of the tournament, the corresponding market will resolve to "No".

If the 2026 PPA: Sacramento Open Mixed Doubles Tournament is cancelled, postponed after April 28, 2026 ET, or there is otherwise no winner declared within that timeframe, this market will resolve to "Other".

The primary resolution source will be official information from the Professional Pickleball Association (https://ppatour.com/); however, a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

eventMetadata.context_description: Eric Oncins and Tyra Hurricane Black clinched the Mixed Doubles Pro Main Draw title at the 2026 PPA Sacramento Open, securing 100% trader consensus on Polymarket as official results confirm their championship in the winners circle. Their dominant run featured convincing straight-game victories over top contenders, including Andrei Daescu/Parris Todd in the semifinals (5-8) and Lindsey Newman/Tyler Loong, highlighted by stifling defense that held opponents to minimal points and exploiting stylistic matchups with precise dinking and powerful smashes. Absent the usual powerhouse Johns/Waters duo, their pre-tournament seeding, recent form synergy, and bracket path elevated them as heavy favorites; post-victory, no realistic challenges remain barring rare resolution disputes from official PPA scoring reviews.
